names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Μεθόδιος ο εκ Ρωσίας», with the rank words left off.

The name as days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 1527 gives it, «Мефодий Пешношский, игумен», with the grade taken off. Measured with the gate's own fold before it was written: 'мефодии пешношскии' has no other holder. The name page spells it Пешношский and the day line the same; the kontakion's heading on the same page spells it Песношского, and the name page's spelling is what is stored.

death.note: saint.gr's head line reads «Οσιος Μεθοδιος ο Εκ Ρωσιας (; - 1392)» and the entry says he fell asleep in peace in 1392. The page gives no year of birth and dates his life to the fourteenth century.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 4 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Мефодия , игумена Пешношского (1392).»

attestations.note: The day's second entry of eleven, «Прп. Мефодия , игумена Пешношского (1392).», which gives him the abbot's grade this folder already carries in `types` and the year 1392 it already holds. Only the Greek row stood before this, so the identification rests on the menologion day, the Пешношский epithet and the abbot's grade together, and this is the folder's first Cyrillic name form. The day page prints a troparion and a kontakion under his name and both are added; the troparion calls him the fellow-faster and fellow-talker of «преподобному Сергию», which is a statement inside a hymn and not a `related` row: `related-floor.mjs` reads `life.md` prose only, so no row is owed and none was written. The page spells the epithet two ways in two headings, Пешношского over the troparion and Песношского over the kontakion, and each is quoted as printed. `life1303` was NOT read. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Μεθόδιος ο εκ Ρωσίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and does not carry the «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. saint.gr's head line dates him «(; - 1392)» and the entry is two sentences. The monastery of Peshnosha, near Dmitrov in the province of Moscow, is named, and `locations` is left out. He is a Russian saint and the Russian calendar was not opened for this draft, which is what the `russian` row's note says. The corpus keeps a `methodius-of-patara` and nobody of Peshnosha. No hymn is printed.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).

hymns.text: Божественною любовию от юности распаляемь,/ вся, яже в мире красная, возненавидев,/ Христа Единаго возлюбил еси,/ и, сего ради в пустыню вселився,/ в ней обитель сотворил еси,/ и, собрав инок множество,/ приял еси от Бога чудес дар, отче Мефодие,/ и был еси о Христе собеседник и спостник преподобному Сергию,/ с нимже у Христа Бога испроси православным христианом здравие, и спасение,/ и душам нашим велию милость.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Тропарь преподобного Мефодия, игумена Пешношского», глас 8, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 4 июня ст. ст.. It names him in the vocative, so it is his own proper, and it names the venerable Sergius with him.

english.text: Set afire with divine love from thy youth, thou didst hate all that is fair in the world and didst love Christ alone; and for His sake thou wentest to dwell in the wilderness and madest a monastery in it, and gathering a multitude of monks thou didst receive from God the gift of wonders, O father Methodius. And thou wast in Christ the companion in speech and in fasting of the venerable Sergius: with him ask of Christ God health and salvation for Orthodox Christians, and great mercy for our souls.

hymns.text: Послушания добрый рачитель быв,/ безплотныя враги слезными молитвами твоими крепко посрамил еси/ и явился еси Пресвятыя Троицы жилище,/ Юже зря, блаженне, ясно,/ Богомудре Мефодие преподобне,/ чудес дар от Нея приял еси./ Темже исцелявши с верою приходящих недуги,/ утолявши скорби/ и молишися непрестанно о всех нас.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Кондак преподобного Мефодия, игумена Песношского», глас 4, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 4 июня ст. ст.. The heading spells the epithet Песношского where the troparion's spells it Пешношского, and it is quoted as printed. It names him in the vocative.

english.text: A good lover of obedience wast thou, and with thy tearful prayers thou didst mightily shame the bodiless enemies and wast shown to be a dwelling of the Most Holy Trinity; and beholding Her clearly, O blessed and God-wise venerable Methodius, thou didst receive from Her the gift of wonders. Therefore thou healest the ailments of those who come in faith, and stillest their sorrows, and prayest unceasingly for us all.
